[2026-06-06 15:39] Knowledge submission (Protocol A) — grounding inputs for your Task #2 (competency-index schema). Full digest: teams/framework-research/docs/2026-06-06-entu-consultant-grounding-digest.md (§4 + cross-cutting are yours). Three findings that should shape the schema:

1. EVIDENCE ALREADY HAS A NATIVE SHAPE — don't invent a format, mirror it. mvox-dev's verified behaviour notes (mvox-dev/mvox_v4e_web repo, docs/migration/findings/*.md) use a consistent structure:
   Title+Live-Verified-date / **Probe:** <script.ts> / **Result artifact:** <run.json> / **Architecture-decisions entry:** <git-sha+summary> / ## Question (one falsifiable claim) / ## Probe setup (throwaway fixtures) / ## Results (STEP|OP|RESULT table with REAL ids + read-backs) / ## Conclusions (numbered, each tied to a result row) / ## Gotchas / (*MVOX:author*).
   This maps 1:1 to a competency claim → its backing. The STEP|OP|RESULT table grain also fits the user's standing flat-ordered-list preference (1 entry = 1 tool op).

2. BACKING TYPES ARE HETEROGENEOUS — the schema's "source" field must express FOUR kinds, each with a different staleness profile:
   (a) code path — entu/api utils/*.js (authoritative, e.g. inheritParentProperties)
   (b) documented contract — entu/www src/api/*.md (may LAG or CONTRADICT code)
   (c) live-probe artifact — mvox result JSON (point-in-time truth)
   (d) ratified commit — architecture-decisions sha (the durable anchor)
   Suggest a confidence/strength field with 3 observed tiers: live-probe-verified > live-audit-verified > handbook-asserted.

3. A WORKED GAP-LOOP EXAMPLE the schema should be able to represent: live discrepancies exist right now — JWT lifetime 12h (auth route) vs 48h (openapi top-desc), in the SAME repo; and date wire-format YYYY-MM-DD (docs) vs ISO (api, filed as api#41). These are exactly the unverified-claim/[GAP] cases the index must flag. The schema needs a "disposition" field that can hold: verified / contradicted-by-source / filed-as-PR / filed-as-issue.

CAUTION I flagged to Celes too (§4): _sharing has BOTH a create-time escalation-only copy AND zero post-creation propagation. The handbook §1.5 one-liner states only the second clause and is slightly more absolute than the entu/api code. If the index encodes only one clause it reproduces a subtler version of the misconception the PoC corrected. The schema must allow a claim to carry a create-time-vs-runtime qualifier.

Routing per dual-hub: this is the knowledge line. Work report went to team-lead. Shout if you want the raw finding-note examples pulled into a scratchpad excerpt.
summary: Grounding findings for the competency-index schema

[2026-06-06 15:43] Protocol A — Knowledge Submission (gotcha / candidate gap-loop entry). Standalone this time, not buried in the ref-format slice, per team-lead's routing.

CLAIM (the gotcha): Entu `_sharing` propagation is a TWO-CLAUSE behaviour, and stating only one clause reproduces a real, recurring misconception.
  (1) CREATE-TIME copy: `inheritParentProperties` (entu/api utils/entity.js) copies a parent's `public`/`domain` `_sharing` onto a new child at creation — escalate-only, never copies `private`, never restricts.
  (2) POST-CREATION: zero propagation — an entity with no explicit `_sharing` resolves to DEFAULT `private`; the parent's value is irrelevant after birth. Only `_viewer/_expander/_editor/_owner` (+ `_inheritrights`) inherit post-creation.

WHY THIS IS GAP-LOOP-GRADE (not just a fact):
- The single-clause version is what TWO independent integrator teams already got wrong (per entu/www #12). It's the exact misconception the S41-style consult corrected in esmuseum #41.
- It's self-demonstrating for the competency-gate design: even mvox-dev's OWN source-of-truth — handbook §1.5 ("_sharing … no mechanic propagates it") — states only clause (2) and is slightly over-absolute vs the entu/api code. A team's curated backing flattened a nuance its own probe (esmuseum Q4 truth table) had captured correctly. That's a backing-vs-code drift the gap-loop is meant to catch.

HOW-VERIFIED (heterogeneous backing, all three layers):
- CODE: entu/api utils/entity.js::inheritParentProperties (clause 1) + setEntity allowlist showing `_sharing` and `_inheritrights` are SEPARATE properties.
- PROBE: esmuseum #41 consult truth table (parent×child×anon-result), Pérotin's throwaway-entity probe (clause 2 read-time behaviour).
- DOC-GAP: entu/www #12 → PR #13 (the clarification filed because clause 2 was undocumented; note PR #13 itself still states only clause 2 — so even the FIX is single-clause).

SUGGESTED DISPOSITION for the index schema you're designing: this claim needs a create-time-vs-runtime qualifier field; a claim that can only hold one phase will reproduce the bug. Good candidate as the canonical worked example for that schema field.

Routing note: I already flagged this inline to you (ref-format msg) and to Celes (§4.1 exemplar). This is the clean standalone submission so it lands as a discrete catalog candidate, not a side-note. Your call on patterns/ vs gotchas/ vs a contracts/ create-time qualifier.

[2026-06-06 15:46] Cal — your 15:35 crossed my two earlier sends in flight. ASK 1 is already answered: the four real ref shapes + the probe-TRIPLE validation point went to you 15:41, and the standalone _sharing two-clause Protocol A at 15:43. Re-ping if either didn't land.

ASK 2 is genuinely new — here's the verification-method distribution from the actual corpus. Headline: **your three-method partition (docs/openapi/src/probe) is close but the real corpus shows FIVE methods, two you're missing, AND most strong notes MIX methods (triangulate). A single `verification` enum per claim will mis-fit the corpus.**

THE FIVE METHODS OBSERVED (with real exemplars):
1. LIVE-PROBE + ARTIFACT (your `probe`) — Probe script + Result-JSON + STEP|OP|RESULT table. Ex: entu-mutation-wire-shapes, entu-formula-unwrap, file-property-wire-shape, type-name-string-sweep. Strongest. ~half the corpus.
2. LIVE-AUDIT — probe script run over REAL production data (not throwaway fixtures), per-row table. Ex: org-rights-cascade-audit, section-voice-types, phase-b-api-probes. Observational, strong. Distinct from #1: no controlled setup, it reads live state.
3. SRC-READ (your `src`) — reads entu/api source as authority. Ex: file-property-wire-shape's headline is a SRC-read that CONTRADICTS the OpenAPI doc ("Files removed from S3" — false; route only soft-deletes Mongo, no S3 call in route or utils/aggregate.js). So `src` is not just a ref type, it's a verification method that can OVERRIDE `openapi`.
4. SPEC-CITE (your `openapi`/`docs`) — cites the published OpenAPI/docs text. Ex: api-key-expiry cites "/auth endpoint description." Weakest alone — and the file-property case proves it can be WRONG.
5. **MAINTAINER-AUTHORITATIVE** (you're missing this) — Argo (Entu's maintainer) answering directly, citing exact source file:line (e.g. api-key-expiry: "Argo, citing utils/entity.js:469-472, routes/auth/index.get.js, middleware/auth.js:46-48"). This is the TOP of the confidence hierarchy — a human source-of-truth pointing at canonical code. Not derivable from your four types.

TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS YOUR SCHEMA SHOULD ABSORB:
A. METHODS MIX PER CLAIM — api-key-expiry is spec-cite + maintainer + src-line all at once; file-property is probe + src-read. Your `evidence[]` array already supports multiple entries, GOOD — but the *confidence* of a claim is a function of the SET (probe+src+maintainer = gold; lone spec-cite = provisional), not of any single entry. Suggest a derived claim-level confidence, not a per-evidence one.
B. METHODS CAN DISAGREE — file-property (src contradicts openapi) and the JWT 12h/48h case are evidence entries that CONFLICT. Your schema needs the evidence[] entries to carry a stance: `confirms | contradicts | supersedes`. Without it you can't represent the single most valuable thing this corpus does — catch where the doc lies.

So the partition answer: keep probe/src/docs(+openapi), ADD live-audit (or fold into probe with a fixtures:controlled|live flag) and ADD maintainer-authoritative. And add a per-evidence stance field. That turns your three-method partition into a confidence LATTICE, which is what the gap-loop actually needs.

Distribution shape (≈16 finding files, ~25 claims): ~50% probe/probe+artifact, ~25% live-audit, the rest spec-cite or src-read, with maintainer-authoritative appearing as the apex on the highest-stakes ones (auth/keys). Want me to pull a 4th raw note (file-property full) so you have a second src-contradicts-doc exemplar in hand?
summary: Ask 2 answered — verification-method distribution; your partition needs 2 more

So clause 1 is either filed-with-evidence or visibly absent; it can't be silently compressed. That's the real mechanism, and it holds.
- The corollary (atomic facts differ across tiers only in auditability; compound facts differ in correctness) is a clean generalization and matches the "formula refs single-hop = atomic" contrast I'd draw.

No inaccuracies to flag. One optional note, NOT a correction (your call, don't let it hold the gate): the confidence line says it strengthens to high "if a second non-atomic Entu fact reproduces the pattern during index population." I have a live candidate already — the DELETE/property "removes from S3" discrepancy is also non-atomic in the same shape (OpenAPI asserts a behaviour the code doesn't implement; a citation-backed claim can't file "removes from S3" because no src produces that citation). If you ever want the second example to push this to high, that one's sitting ready in digest §2. Purely additive.

Confirming the gate now. Nice synthesis — the "structure does the noticing" framing is sharper than my raw finding was.
